transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-08
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Lina Torres (Redwood CSM), Rajesh Patel (Sentinel VP Eng), Marta Lopez (Sentinel SRE), Tom Nguyen (Sentinel CTO)

Summary: quick postmortem follow-up; confirm fixes, action items, and security artifacts to close the escalation

----- Transcript -----
[00:00] Jared: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 40 minutes. Quick round of intros?
[00:08] Rajesh: hi, yeah Rajesh here, VP engineering at Sentinel. Marta is our SRE, Tom here too.
[00:13] Marta: hi all.
[00:15] Lina: thanks team, Lina from Redwood customer success; main goal today is to close the loop on the incident on Dec 2 and outline next steps.
[00:22] Tom: sounds good.
[00:25] Maya: hi, Maya from SE, I led the runbooks for the incident response. I can walk through the timeline and the mitigation notes.

[00:35] Rajesh: yeah we wanna make sure the fix is robust, and also we need the compliance materials for our audit -- the procurement team is pushing.

[00:42] Maya: ok timeline quick: at 02:12 UTC on Dec 2 we saw the initial error spike, 502s and token timeouts on batch endpoints; then between 02:15-02:40 latency increased across a subset of customers, Sentinel being high on QPS for that window.
[01:05] Marta: and our dashboards showed repeated KV cache misses leading to longer decode times - the cache was being invalidated and then the runtime re-loaded weights slower than expected.
[01:22] Maya: right, so high-level root cause was a race condition in KV cache invalidation in the serving runtime combined with the autoscaler policy on the Dedicated pool that spun up nodes slower than necessary. Two-factor: cache invalidation + autoscale cold starts.
[01:45] Tom: can you clarify the autoscaler part? we thought autoscaler was configured to burst to 8 nodes, but during the incident it only went to 3.
[01:58] Maya: yeah that was the sync issue; the autoscaler controller didn't see the correct desiredPoolCapacity because the metrics exporter had a gap for ~90s - that exporter gap was tied to a transient network flapping on the management plane in the region (we're still investigating the exact provider-level event). So desired didn't match observed. that caused more cold starts and increased tail latency.
[02:25] Rajesh: ok so two angles: infra/metrics flapping and our cache invalidation bug. Which of those is the real blocker?
[02:33] Maya: both mattered but the cache invalidation was the immediate trigger for token delays; autoscaler amplified the impact. If autoscaler had spun up faster, impact would've been much smaller.
[02:40] Marta: one note, in our logs there were a lot of 429s before 502s - rate limiter and retry loops compounded the backlog. maybe we should revisit our client-side retries.
[02:55] Lina: good point. Jared, do we already have notes for recommended client retry/backoff patterns?
[03:02] Jared: yes we do; I'll share the best-practice snippet after this call.

[03:10] Maya: for the immediate mitigation we pushed hotfix 1) added guardrails in cache invalidation to prevent full invalidation on miss storms, 2) lowered cold-start threshold by tweaking the autoscaler policy to pre-warm a spare node when QPS goes above sentinel's baseline, and 3) temporarily increased rate limit quotas to avoid client-triggered 429 cascades.
[03:38] Rajesh: we saw the hotfix but wanted more assurance - what regression testing was done?
[03:44] Maya: unit + integration test for the invalidation path, we also ran a canary load test in our staging dedicated cluster simulating 2x sentinel QPS for 30 minutes. That testing showed stable latencies and no mass invalidations.
[04:01] Tom: any risk that guardrail could cause stale KV reads? we can't have incorrect outputs.
[04:09] Maya: no, guardrail doesn't allow stale keys beyond TTL; it just prevents wholesale flushes during a detected miss storm. We added additional verification steps to ensure cache coherence.
[04:22] Marta: ok that's better, still would like to run the same test from our side.
[04:27] Maya: absolutely. we'll schedule a joint benchmark on a dedicated pool replica.

[04:33] Rajesh: about root cause for exporter gap - is that on Redwood side or cloud provider? we need that to complete our RCA for internal compliance.
[04:42] Lina: initial tracing suggests management-plane packet loss; we're working with provider. we'll share any provider incident reports and packet captures where allowed.
[04:50] Tom: please do, procurement/legal will want that.

[04:56] Maya: couple of reliability items we propose long-term: 1) enable kv cache replication across availability sets so invalidation events are localized, 2) add predictive pre-warming based on traffic patterns, 3) expose autoscaler health signals to Sentinel's SRE dashboards.
[05:14] Rajesh: replication sounds good. any cost implications?
[05:19] Jared: yep replication will add some network and memory overhead; we'll run a cost estimate and include tradeoffs - likely a modest percent increase for significant reliability gains.

[05:30] Marta: for our audit we need clear notes on encryption, keys, and logs retention. Lina?
[05:36] Lina: on that - we have SOC2 artifacts and KMS screenshots; I'll attach those to the support ticket. Also redwood provides optional HSM integrations for Private deployments, we can discuss if Sentinel wants that.
[05:50] Tom: our legal is leaning towards Private or Dedicated with strict KMS handling. can you share options and pricing?
[05:58] Jared: yes I'll send Dedicated commitment tiers and Private deployment pricing matrix.

[06:05] Rajesh: any follow-up on mitigations side - are there open bugs or PRs?
[06:12] Maya: open PRs: cache-guard-271 (merged to canary, in prod as hotfix), autoscaler-expose-88 (ops config change, rolled out to 2 regions), exporter-reconnect-45 (retry logic for metrics exporter, in PR). We flagged exporter-reconnect as priority for provider coord.
[06:33] Marta: can you share the PR links? sometimes fireflies transcribed as link placeholders - but ideally we get direct github links.
[06:41] Lina: yes we'll paste links into the ticket.

[06:45] Rajesh: about detection - we want earlier alerting on KV miss storms, is there a new alert threshold recommended?
[06:52] Maya: recommend adding an alert for sustained cache miss rate > 5% for 2 minutes and a secondary for miss bursts > 20% in 30s. We'll provide the exact prometheus rules.
[07:06] Tom: good. also can we get sampling of inference outputs during high latency windows for QA? we need to verify no degradation.
[07:14] Maya: we'll add sampling hooks; note we redact PII before shipping samples - need Rajesh to confirm fields.
[07:23] Rajesh: yep we'll provide a list of allowed fields.

[07:28] (short pause)
[07:31] Jared: quick check - any outstanding exec asks?
[07:35] Tom: just the compliance pack and confirmation on the Dedicated commit cost.

[07:40] Lina: ok to recap next steps: Redwood to send final postmortem doc, share PR links and provider incident report if/when available, schedule joint benchmark, and attach SOC2/KMS screenshots to ticket.
[07:56] Rajesh: timeline for postmortem doc?
[07:59] Lina: we'll aim EOD 12/09 for the TL;DR and full doc by 12/10.
[08:06] Maya: for the benchmark I'll coordinate with Marta; propose week of 12/14.
[08:12] Marta: that works.

[08:15] Jared: ok anything else on reliability improvements?
[08:18] Rajesh: one more ask: can we get a simple SLA credit calculation example for incidents like this?
[08:24] Jared: yes I'll include an example scenario in the follow-up.

[08:29] Tom: also re: competitors - just FYI procurement asked us to look at Anthropic and Bedrock for price/perf; we're primarily with you but they'll compare.
[08:41] Jared: understood. we'll include comparative notes but main focus is mitigation and closure.

[08:46] Lina: ok let's move to action items review.
[08:50] Maya: action 1: run KV cache replication tests and share logs (owner: Maya) - target 12/15.
[08:58] Lina: action 2: upload SOC2 and KMS screenshots (owner: Lina) - target 12/10.
[09:05] Jared: action 3: send Dedicated pricing and Private options (owner: Jared) - target 12/12.
[09:12] Rajesh: action 4: confirm PII fields for sample outputs (owner: Rajesh) - target 12/11.

[09:20] Marta: last tech question - will the guardrail change affect model warmup times for very long contexts? we rely on longer seq lengths sometimes.
[09:30] Maya: we tuned guardrail to preserve warmup semantics; longer contexts still trigger full kv fills but guardrail prevents blanket flushes. we can share microbenchmarks.

[09:44] Tom: thanks everyone.
[09:47] Lara: (note: speaker label mis-attribution)
[09:50] Jared: thanks all, we'll follow up with the doc and ticket attachments.
[09:55] Rajesh: thanks.
[10:00] (call ends)

----- End Transcript -----
